identity.name: BANSWARA SYNTEX LIMITED
identity.industry: Integrated Textiles — Yarn / Fabric / Garments (worsted & synthetic blended)

summary.oneLiner: Vertically integrated Indian textile manufacturer operating through three divisions - Yarn, Fabric and Garments - serving domestic and export markets.
summary.business: Banswara Syntex Limited is a vertically integrated textile manufacturer with three integrated business divisions - Yarn, Fabric and Garments. Its diversified product portfolio spans spun synthetic blended yarn, wool and wool-mix yarn, worsted and synthetic fabrics, cotton and linen fabrics, technical textiles, shirting fabrics and readymade garments, sold to domestic and international customers. Exports accounted for 47% of FY26 turnover (up from 44% in FY25).

currentContext.business: Banswara Syntex Limited is a vertically integrated textile manufacturer with three integrated business divisions - Yarn, Fabric and Garments. Its diversified product portfolio spans spun synthetic blended yarn, wool and wool-mix yarn, worsted and synthetic fabrics, cotton and linen fabrics, technical textiles, shirting fabrics and readymade garments, sold to domestic and international customers. Exports accounted for 47% of FY26 turnover (up from 44% in FY25).

currentContext.strengths: Vertically integrated manufacturing model across Yarn, Fabric and Garment divisions enabling operational synergies across the textile value chain|Shifting mix toward higher-value-add Fabric and Garment divisions, which management expects to drive future growth and profitability|Export orientation with 47% of FY26 turnover from exports (up from 44% in FY25)
currentContext.strategies: Growth strategy centred on increasing domestic consumption of fabrics and garments and expanding opportunities in global textile and apparel markets|Strengthening the divisional structure with focused growth strategies for each of the Yarn, Fabric and Garment businesses|Expanding the contribution of the Fabric and Garment divisions, which offer higher value addition and stronger margin potential, expected to lead future growth and profitability|Expanding domestic market presence, strengthening relationships with global customers, increasing penetration in global markets, improving operational efficiencies and enhancing product mix through greater emphasis on value-added textiles and garments
currentContext.expansion: The Company invested Rs. 8,849 Lakhs during FY26 (previous year Rs. 14,694 Lakhs) for modernization of its production capacities, with capital-work-in-progress of Rs. 3,016 Lakhs and advances to capital goods suppliers of Rs. 1,535 Lakhs outstanding at year-end, indicating continuing modernization spend rather than a single named project. Separately, the Company operates two captive Thermal Power Plants of 33 MW total capacity, both reported as working satisfactorily, meeting coal requirements from domestic sources.
currentContext.mdna: Improving demand trends in key export markets and a gradual recovery in retail consumption support medium-term growth prospects|Anticipated benefits from international trade agreements and ongoing customer additions across key markets expected to support growth in coming years|Global supply chain diversification and the continuing China+1 sourcing strategy have strengthened India's position as a preferred textile manufacturing destination|Government initiatives promoting investments, exports and manufacturing competitiveness expected to provide further support to the sector over the medium term|FY26 profitability improvement driven by better sales realizations, stronger contribution from value-added products, improved product mix, higher revenue contribution from Fabric and Garment divisions, enhanced operating efficiencies and better fixed-cost absorption|Continuing headwinds from elevated raw material costs, higher employee expenses from wage revisions, labour shortages in certain operations, geopolitical uncertainties and disruptions in select export markets impacted demand visibility and operating performance in certain segments

risks.note: Fluctuations in raw material prices, particularly cotton, man-made fibres, dyes and chemicals, may adversely impact operating margins.

Global economic uncertainties, geopolitical developments, inflationary pressures and changing trade policies can affect demand in key export markets; during FY26 the Company faced disruptions in select export markets.
The industry faces challenges from increasing energy and logistics costs that can pressure operating margins.
Flagged as an industry-wide risk affecting a textile manufacturer with material export turnover (47% of FY26 turnover).
Stringent environmental and sustainability compliance requirements pose an ongoing cost/compliance risk to operations.
The textile industry operates in a highly competitive environment with intense competition from both domestic and international players, which can pressure pricing and margins.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption and labour shortages
risks.note: Supply chain disruptions and labour shortages were cited as challenges to business performance; FY26 results were also impacted by labour shortages in certain operations and higher employee expenses from wage revisions.

risks.risk: Reliance on bank borrowings and public fixed deposits for funding
risks.note: During FY26 the Company drew fresh loan disbursements of Rs. 5,906.28 Lakhs for fixed-asset acquisition while repaying Rs. 5,875 Lakhs of term loans, and carried outstanding public fixed deposits of Rs. 1,803 Lakhs as at 31 March 2026, indicating dependence on external bank and deposit funding for capex and working capital.

thesis (one line): Vertically-integrated worsted/synthetic textile mill pivoting revenue mix toward higher-margin Fabric + Garment (66%→target 70%), riding China+1/weak-INR competitiveness and large export customer additions (Walmart), while battling labor shortages in spinning, wool/polyester cost inflation and elevated debt.
scorecard:
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | Q4 FY25 | YoY | FY26 | FY25 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total income | INR 369.3 cr | — | — | ~INR 1,370 cr | — | — | — |
| Yarn revenue | INR 113 cr | INR 123 cr | −8% (−INR10cr) | INR 449 cr | INR 460 cr | −2% | Labor/util drag |
| Fabric revenue | INR 154 cr | INR 145 cr | +6% | INR 569 cr (record) | — | +5% | Premium/wool-blend traction |
| Garment revenue | INR 96 cr | ~INR 69 cr | +40% | INR 324 cr | — | +18% | Walmart ~INR15cr of Q4 |
| EBITDA | INR 46 cr | ~INR 31.5 cr | +46% | ~INR 144 cr | ~INR 117.6 cr | +22.5% | Margin ~11% FY26 |
| PAT (reported) | INR 9.6 cr | ~INR 5.1 cr | +87% | INR 28.4 cr | ~INR 21.4 cr | +32.8% | — |
| PAT (normalized) | — | — | — | ~INR 37.4 cr | — | — | Add back ~INR9cr one-off |
| Volume — Yarn | 46 lakh kg | — | — | 194 lakh kg | — | — | Util 78% Q4 / 77% FY |
| Volume — Fabric | 62 lakh m | — | — | 230 lakh m | — | — | Util 77% Q4 |
| Volume — Garment | 11 lakh pcs | — | — | 39 lakh pcs | — | — | Util 72% FY (vs ~50% FY25) |
| Net debt | — | — | — | INR 483 cr | INR 456 cr (FY25) | +INR27cr | D/E 0.8x |

**One-offs:** INR ~9 cr one-time exceptional expense (new labor code law implementation). Reported PAT INR28.4cr is AFTER this charge.
**Fabric+Garment mix:** 66% of revenue (FY26) vs 63% (FY25); medium-term target ~70%.
**Realizations:** Yarn realization +INR30–35/kg YoY (value-added mix, dyed Siro Compact Spandex). Fabric value/meter up (worsted), though full pass-through still pending.
**Dividend:** 20% on face value; total payout INR 3.42 cr.
**Tesca JV:** ~INR100cr turnover, ~INR10cr PAT; Banswara's 40% share ~INR4cr.
guidance (critical — explicit):
- **FY27 revenue:** INR 1,450–1,500 cr (from ~INR1,370cr FY26); growth led by Fabric + Garment.
- **Segment growth FY27:** Fabric ~20% and Garment ~18–20% targeted (Garment to ~INR400cr, capacity could support ~INR450cr).
- **EBITDA margin:** 10.5%–11% over medium-term. NEAR-TERM margins may DIP as RM cost pass-through lags (H1 FY27 volatile; H2 stronger, as usual).
- **Value-added mix:** Fabric+Garment 66%→~70% medium-term.
- **Capex FY27:** INR 135–140 cr — mostly Yarn + Fabric + sustainability (zero-liquid-discharge, 132 KVA line); Garment only INR3–5cr (machines exist, just worker training).
- **Longer term:** INR2,000cr revenue achievable "without significant capex" (no firm timeline given geopolitics); peak INR1,800cr possibly FY28/FY29.
- **Debt:** No reduction in FY27 (planned capex); long-term debt reduction begins FY28 onward.
demand / order book:
- US & Europe export demand "relatively stable"; healthy domestic demand.
- Garment order book healthy; Walmart added (~INR15cr of Q4 Garment), more replenishment expected.
- **Caution:** Q1 FY27 Garment demand visibility weak/subdued (geopolitics + RM costs; brands cautious); recovery expected from Q2 onward.
- Middle East demand sluggish — INR8–9cr of shipments slipped in Q4; total ME exposure ~INR100cr, expects INR10–20cr reduction in FY27.
segment detail:
- **Yarn:** Headwinds from labor shortages (spinning) → util 77–78%; persisting into Q1 FY27 (still a problem in May). Strategy: run finer counts (Siro Compact ~200 t/month) when labor scarce — lower kg output but higher value. Internal: ~33% of yarn supplied to Fabric.
- **Fabric:** Record FY26 revenue INR569cr (+5%); premium/wool-blend + US traction; brands Simone Federico & Figli, Siro. ~25% of fabric goes internally to Garment. Worsted machine investments add value, not meters.
- **Garment:** Star performer — Q4 +40%, FY +18%; util 72% (vs ~50%). ~80% of fabric used is in-house. Capacity ~70k pcs/month (jackets), using only 40–50k. Surat SEZ (40–50k jackets + 100k pants) pending approval — adds capacity when cleared.
growth / optionality:
- China+1 / import-substitution: weak INR (depreciated ~6–7%) + strong Yuan → India competitive vs China in spun-synthetic; substituting Chinese imports domestically.
- FTAs: India-UK FTA expected ~September; EU FTA target by Dec-end — could lift export inquiries.
- Walmart relationship — "infinite" room to grow; deepening with ~6–7 large export anchors (Celio/France, M&S/UK, Mango, JC Penney; engaging Japan).
- Predictive-analytics / AI-led shift from made-to-order → never-out-of-stock to cut lead-times.
- One Mile D2C brand: ~INR15 lakh/month sales; will scale to ~INR1cr/month before raising separate funds (kept off main P&L).
- Tesca JV automotive momentum; intend to add finishing capacity (no stake increase — partners won't dilute).
margins & cost:
- EBITDA margin ~11% FY26 (+22.5% EBITDA growth) despite cost inflation — driven by cost reductions, product mix, better fixed-cost absorption.
- Cost pressure: polyester RM +~25% (petrochem/Middle East); wool fiber up sharply (even more than synthetic — biggest challenge), chemicals/dyestuffs, energy.
- Pass-through lag: customers/retail brands re-price only every ~6–12 months (season pricing) → 2–4 quarter lag; exports easier to pass via INR depreciation.
- Segment EBITDA not disclosed (heavy inter-segment transfers; mgmt views company at "global optima," ~similar to company-level ~11%).
capex:
- FY26 invested ~INR30cr Yarn + ~INR40cr Fabric (upgrades; installed capacity optically down due to finer-count product shift).
- FY27: INR135–140cr — Yarn, Fabric, sustainability (ZLD, 132 KVA line); Garment minimal (INR3–5cr).
- Surat SEZ garment capacity awaiting SEZ/Kandla approval; possible mid-year (Q2/Q3) incremental garment expansion if momentum builds (low capex).
capital allocation / debt:
- Net debt INR483cr (vs INR456cr FY25); +INR27cr from working capital (deliberate — ready inventory for customers) + machinery modernization. D/E 0.8x (comfortable).
- FY27: debt likely to stay elevated/rise (capex-driven, long-term). Reduction from FY28 onward (loans have 5–7 yr tenure, amortize gradually).
- Dividend 20% face value (INR3.42cr payout).
- Watching aged inventory (>90 days).
risks:
- **Labor shortage** in spinning/garmenting — structural-ish (Apr–Jun de facto), constrains utilization & ramp.
- **Commodity:** wool + polyester + energy inflation; pass-through lag squeezes near-term margin.
- **Geopolitics / Middle East:** shipping (Jebel Ali→Fujairah trucking), freight/insurance, demand drop (~INR10–20cr ME revenue at risk).
- **Demand:** Q1 FY27 Garment cautious; brand reorder uncertainty.
- **Debt/working capital** elevated; FX/INR volatility (double-edged — helps exports, raises import RM cost).
- Execution risk on predictive-analytics pivot; Surat SEZ approval timing uncertain.
management tone: Resilient/measured-optimistic. Repeatedly stresses "realistic" and deliberately conservative guidance ("you will hold us to what we say"). Confident on China+1 competitiveness and Garment/Walmart traction; candid on labor, ME, and pass-through lag being lived-with realities. Holistic "global optima" framing over segmental optimization.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Installed capacity optically DOWN YoY despite capex — because finer counts / worsted upgrades trade volume for value (not a red flag).
- Reported PAT understated by ~INR9cr labor-code one-off → normalized PAT ~INR37cr.
- INR depreciation is a margin shock-absorber on exports — no price increase needed to protect garment/fabric export margins.
- Walmart engagement framed as near-infinite runway for a small company; deepen-existing > acquire-new in full-package garment supply.
- Tesca (40% auto JV) quietly contributing ~INR4cr PAT share — hidden value.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- China+1 / weak-INR vs strong-Yuan → Indian spun-synthetic exporters incl. Banswara ⭐ (import-substitution + export share gain).
- India-UK / India-EU FTAs (Sep / Dec-end target) → garment & fabric exporters ✅.
- (No specific external listed-name beneficiaries called out.)

---
qoq log: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Q4 strong — Garment +40% (Walmart onboarded, ~INR15cr), Fabric record FY569cr, EBITDA +46% Q4 / +22.5% FY (~11% margin), PAT +87% Q4 / +32.8% FY (INR9cr labor-code one-off). FY27 guide INR1,450–1,500cr, margin 10.5–11%, capex INR135–140cr. Net debt INR483cr (D/E 0.8x). Labor shortage in spinning persists; ME export softening; wool/polyester inflation with 2–4Q pass-through lag. Prior-call Fabric+Garment 15–20% growth guidance reaffirmed.

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Banswara Syntex Limited is a vertically integrated textile manufacturer with three integrated business divisions - Yarn, Fabric and Garments. Its diversified product portfolio spans spun synthetic blended yarn, wool and wool-mix yarn, worsted and synthetic fabrics, cotton and linen fabrics, technical textiles, shirting fabrics and readymade garments, sold to domestic and international customers. Exports accounted for 47% of FY26 turnover (up from 44% in FY25).

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Banswara Brands Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary, acquired/incorporated 23/08/2022; 100% shareholding
- Tesca Textiles & Seat Components (India) Private Limited — JV: Joint Venture; Company holds 40.64% of paid-up share capital, associated since 20/01/2012; balance held by TESCA Group, France (50.79%) and Kolon Glotech India Private Limited (8.57%); produces laminated/vinyl fabric and embossing panels for the seating/interiors segment

segment_detail.title: Segment detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Yarn:** Headwinds from labor shortages (spinning) → util 77–78%; persisting into Q1 FY27 (still a problem in May). Strategy: run finer counts (Siro Compact ~200 t/month) when labor scarce — lower kg output but higher value. Internal: ~33% of yarn supplied to Fabric.
- **Fabric:** Record FY26 revenue INR569cr (+5%); premium/wool-blend + US traction; brands Simone Federico & Figli, Siro. ~25% of fabric goes internally to Garment. Worsted machine investments add value, not meters.
- **Garment:** Star performer — Q4 +40%, FY +18%; util 72% (vs ~50%). ~80% of fabric used is in-house. Capacity ~70k pcs/month (jackets), using only 40–50k. Surat SEZ (40–50k jackets + 100k pants) pending approval — adds capacity when cleared.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Yarn:** spun synthetic blended yarn, wool and wool-mix yarn
- **Fabric:** worsted and synthetic fabrics, cotton and linen fabrics, technical textiles, shirting fabrics
- **Garment:** readymade garments

order_book.title: Demand / Order book
order_book.body:
- US & Europe export demand "relatively stable"; healthy domestic demand.
- Garment order book healthy; Walmart added (~INR15cr of Q4 Garment), more replenishment expected.
- **Caution:** Q1 FY27 Garment demand visibility weak/subdued (geopolitics + RM costs; brands cautious); recovery expected from Q2 onward.
- Middle East demand sluggish — INR8–9cr of shipments slipped in Q4; total ME exposure ~INR100cr, expects INR10–20cr reduction in FY27.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — explicit)
guidance.body:
- **FY27 revenue:** INR 1,450–1,500 cr (from ~INR1,370cr FY26); growth led by Fabric + Garment.
- **Segment growth FY27:** Fabric ~20% and Garment ~18–20% targeted (Garment to ~INR400cr, capacity could support ~INR450cr).
- **EBITDA margin:** 10.5%–11% over medium-term. NEAR-TERM margins may DIP as RM cost pass-through lags (H1 FY27 volatile; H2 stronger, as usual).
- **Value-added mix:** Fabric+Garment 66%→~70% medium-term.
- **Capex FY27:** INR 135–140 cr — mostly Yarn + Fabric + sustainability (zero-liquid-discharge, 132 KVA line); Garment only INR3–5cr (machines exist, just worker training).
- **Longer term:** INR2,000cr revenue achievable "without significant capex" (no firm timeline given geopolitics); peak INR1,800cr possibly FY28/FY29.
- **Debt:** No reduction in FY27 (planned capex); long-term debt reduction begins FY28 onward.

growth_optionality.title: Growth / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- China+1 / import-substitution: weak INR (depreciated ~6–7%) + strong Yuan → India competitive vs China in spun-synthetic; substituting Chinese imports domestically.
- FTAs: India-UK FTA expected ~September; EU FTA target by Dec-end — could lift export inquiries.
- Walmart relationship — "infinite" room to grow; deepening with ~6–7 large export anchors (Celio/France, M&S/UK, Mango, JC Penney; engaging Japan).
- Predictive-analytics / AI-led shift from made-to-order → never-out-of-stock to cut lead-times.
- One Mile D2C brand: ~INR15 lakh/month sales; will scale to ~INR1cr/month before raising separate funds (kept off main P&L).
- Tesca JV automotive momentum; intend to add finishing capacity (no stake increase — partners won't dilute).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Improving demand trends in key export markets and a gradual recovery in retail consumption support medium-term growth prospects
- Anticipated benefits from international trade agreements and ongoing customer additions across key markets expected to support growth in coming years
- Global supply chain diversification and the continuing China+1 sourcing strategy have strengthened India's position as a preferred textile manufacturing destination
- Government initiatives promoting investments, exports and manufacturing competitiveness expected to provide further support to the sector over the medium term
- FY26 profitability improvement driven by better sales realizations, stronger contribution from value-added products, improved product mix, higher revenue contribution from Fabric and Garment divisions, enhanced operating efficiencies and better fixed-cost absorption
- Continuing headwinds from elevated raw material costs, higher employee expenses from wage revisions, labour shortages in certain operations, geopolitical uncertainties and disruptions in select export markets impacted demand visibility and operating performance in certain segments

margins.title: Margins & cost
margins.body:
- EBITDA margin ~11% FY26 (+22.5% EBITDA growth) despite cost inflation — driven by cost reductions, product mix, better fixed-cost absorption.
- Cost pressure: polyester RM +~25% (petrochem/Middle East); wool fiber up sharply (even more than synthetic — biggest challenge), chemicals/dyestuffs, energy.
- Pass-through lag: customers/retail brands re-price only every ~6–12 months (season pricing) → 2–4 quarter lag; exports easier to pass via INR depreciation.
- Segment EBITDA not disclosed (heavy inter-segment transfers; mgmt views company at "global optima," ~similar to company-level ~11%).

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation / debt
capital_allocation.body:
- Net debt INR483cr (vs INR456cr FY25); +INR27cr from working capital (deliberate — ready inventory for customers) + machinery modernization. D/E 0.8x (comfortable).
- FY27: debt likely to stay elevated/rise (capex-driven, long-term). Reduction from FY28 onward (loans have 5–7 yr tenure, amortize gradually).
- Dividend 20% face value (INR3.42cr payout).
- Watching aged inventory (>90 days).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company invested Rs. 8,849 Lakhs during FY26 (previous year Rs. 14,694 Lakhs) for modernization of its production capacities, with capital-work-in-progress of Rs. 3,016 Lakhs and advances to capital goods suppliers of Rs. 1,535 Lakhs outstanding at year-end, indicating continuing modernization spend rather than a single named project. Separately, the Company operates two captive Thermal Power Plants of 33 MW total capacity, both reported as working satisfactorily, meeting coal requirements from domestic sources.

management_tone.title: Management tone
management_tone.body: Resilient/measured-optimistic. Repeatedly stresses "realistic" and deliberately conservative guidance ("you will hold us to what we say"). Confident on China+1 competitiveness and Garment/Walmart traction; candid on labor, ME, and pass-through lag being lived-with realities. Holistic "global optima" framing over segmental optimization.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Vertically integrated manufacturing model across Yarn, Fabric and Garment divisions enabling operational synergies across the textile value chain
- Shifting mix toward higher-value-add Fabric and Garment divisions, which management expects to drive future growth and profitability
- Export orientation with 47% of FY26 turnover from exports (up from 44% in FY25)

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- **Labor shortage** in spinning/garmenting — structural-ish (Apr–Jun de facto), constrains utilization & ramp.
- **Commodity:** wool + polyester + energy inflation; pass-through lag squeezes near-term margin.
- **Geopolitics / Middle East:** shipping (Jebel Ali→Fujairah trucking), freight/insurance, demand drop (~INR10–20cr ME revenue at risk).
- **Demand:** Q1 FY27 Garment cautious; brand reorder uncertainty.
- **Debt/working capital** elevated; FX/INR volatility (double-edged — helps exports, raises import RM cost).
- Execution risk on predictive-analytics pivot; Surat SEZ approval timing uncertain.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- Installed capacity optically DOWN YoY despite capex — because finer counts / worsted upgrades trade volume for value (not a red flag).
- Reported PAT understated by ~INR9cr labor-code one-off → normalized PAT ~INR37cr.
- INR depreciation is a margin shock-absorber on exports — no price increase needed to protect garment/fabric export margins.
- Walmart engagement framed as near-infinite runway for a small company; deepen-existing > acquire-new in full-package garment supply.
- Tesca (40% auto JV) quietly contributing ~INR4cr PAT share — hidden value.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Growth strategy centred on increasing domestic consumption of fabrics and garments and expanding opportunities in global textile and apparel markets
- Strengthening the divisional structure with focused growth strategies for each of the Yarn, Fabric and Garment businesses
- Expanding the contribution of the Fabric and Garment divisions, which offer higher value addition and stronger margin potential, expected to lead future growth and profitability
- Expanding domestic market presence, strengthening relationships with global customers, increasing penetration in global markets, improving operational …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries
challenges.body:
- China+1 / weak-INR vs strong-Yuan → Indian spun-synthetic exporters incl. Banswara ⭐ (import-substitution + export share gain).
- India-UK / India-EU FTAs (Sep / Dec-end target) → garment & fabric exporters ✅.
- (No specific external listed-name beneficiaries called out.)

---

qoq_log.title: QoQ Log
qoq_log.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Q4 strong — Garment +40% (Walmart onboarded, ~INR15cr), Fabric record FY569cr, EBITDA +46% Q4 / +22.5% FY (~11% margin), PAT +87% Q4 / +32.8% FY (INR9cr labor-code one-off). FY27 guide INR1,450–1,500cr, margin 10.5–11%, capex INR135–140cr. Net debt INR483cr (D/E 0.8x). Labor shortage in spinning persists; ME export softening; wool/polyester inflation with 2–4Q pass-through lag. Prior-call Fabric+Garment 15–20% growth guidance reaffirmed.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Labour law] Exceptional item of Rs 8.9 crore in FY26 relates to "increase in employee benefit obligations resulting from the change in labour law by the Government of India".
- [FTA] The Company repeatedly cites "operationalization of the Free Trade Agreements" as a growth lever, specifically that the "FTA with UK will increase the share of Indian exports to UK substantially benefiting Banswara's export business in all its divisions".
- [Industry, source IBEF] India is described as the world's second-largest textile producer and sixth-largest exporter with a 4.6% share of global textile and apparel trade; in FY25 the sector contributed 2.3% to GDP, 13% to industrial production and 12% to India's exports.
- [China+1] Deck cites China+1 as increasing demand for Man-Made Fabrics manufactured in India and expects India's textile exports to grow ~11% CAGR to $65 bn by 2026 from $36 bn in 2019.
